purpose: A bounded public-evidence claim review; not an independent source search, user-demand study or model benchmark.

project.purpose: Seven read-only stdio MCP tools for public OSV, NVD, KEV, EPSS and deps.dev lookups. No local repository scanning or dependency graph.
project.record: The repository reports 289 automated tests for v0.1.3. Its validation plan explicitly records no independent-user pilot, repeat-use data or measured comparative workflow benefit.

evidence.summary: A user reported a malware warning for a Git-pinned dependency after matching to a same-name npm registry package. A maintainer discussed commit versus package identity. The issue later closed automatically for staleness; this does not establish a fix.
Maintainers requested the path from a vulnerable transitive dependency to the direct dependency they can change. This is a dependency-graph workflow, beyond a package metadata lookup.

These maintained project or vendor sources document overlapping OSV queries, advisory details, MCP access, source context or structured vulnerability enrichment. Runtime comparative benchmarks were not performed.

FIRST describes EPSS as the probability of observed exploitation activity over the next 30 days across the community. Local assets, exposure and impact are additional inputs. It warns against treating EPSS multiplied by ordinal CVSS as a meaningful combined risk measure.
Current official documentation labels cveId deprecated and recommends cveIds. This review has not established that cveId currently fails.
